messages.subject: bar plot
parts:
Hello,

I have 5 numbers that I want to draw a bar plot for.
I want to create three groups: (a) for the first number (b) for the next two numbers (c) for the next two numbers

|           
|                  |   |                  |
|                  |   |                  |
|                  |   |              |   |
|                  |   |              |   |
                La  Lb          La Lb
Label1       Label2         Label3

La and Lb are two sublabels. I don't want all bars to be together, but separate them somehow visually to three groups. That's my main problem which I am not sure how to do.

Is there a simple way to do that?

Thanks.

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: bar plot
parts:
Besides faceting, you can also try dodging:

dummy <- data.frame(group1 =
c("Label1","Label2","Label2","Label3","Label3"),
group2 = c("","La","Lb","La","Lb"))

ggplot(dummy, aes(x=group1)) + geom_bar(aes(fill=group2),
position="dodge")

or for a little more sophistication:

ggplot(dummy, aes(x=group1)) + geom_bar(aes(fill=group2), width=0.7,
position=position_dodge(width=0.8))

If you don't want different fill colors:

ggplot(dummy, aes(x=group1)) + geom_bar(aes(group=group2), width=0.7,
position=position_dodge(width=0.8))

but then you would have to put the sub-group labels on yourself.

Fills can be greyscale as well:

ggplot(dummy, aes(x=group1)) + geom_bar(aes(fill=group2), width=0.7,
position=position_dodge(width=0.8)) + scale_fill_grey()

--Brian Diggs
